chapter.title: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard

page.h1: HTS Chapter 47: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: What China, India, Mexico & the EU Charge on U.S. Pulp & OCC (HTS Ch. 47) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Rates on U.S. kraft, fluff and dissolving pulp and OCC in 10 markets: 0% in most, 5% in India, 10% extra in China, which bans waste paper, and Canada's 50% on dissolving pulp.

intro: Most of the ten largest markets charge nothing on U.S. wood pulp and recovered paper: the EU, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia at their normal rate, Mexico and Canada under USMCA (and at 0% MFN anyway), and Viet Nam except for 1% on mechanical and dissolving pulp. **India** charges 5% on pulp and 2.5% on recovered paper. **China** adds 10% to its 0% rate on all U.S. goods, 5% more on wood pulp for buyers without an exclusion, and does not let recovered paper in at all. **Canada**'s only surcharge is 50% on dissolving pulp. For recovered paper, access is decided by the buyer's import rules (import licences, pre-shipment inspection, contamination limits), shown on each card; for pulp sold into the EU, by the deforestation rules from December 30, 2026.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: The EU ($1.14B, down 5.4%; Germany, Italy, Poland, the Netherlands and Spain buy most) takes mostly kraft pulp (4703, $864M) and dissolving pulp ($139M), duty-free. What changes is compliance: from December 30, 2026 EU importers must file deforestation due-diligence statements for wood pulp. The U.S. is rated low-risk, so simplified due diligence applies; recovered paper is outside the rules.
profile.mainProducts: Kraft (sulfate) pulp: NBSK, eucalyptus, fluff (4703) · Dissolving pulp (4702)

regulator.name: European Commission (EU Deforestation Regulation 2023/1115; Waste Shipment Regulation 2024/1157)
regulator.requirement: From December 30, 2026 (June 30, 2027 for micro and small firms) the EU importer of wood pulp must file a due-diligence statement that the wood was legally harvested on land not deforested after December 31, 2020, with the geolocation of the harvest plots; recovered paper and pulp made from it are outside the scope. Recovered paper is green-listed waste: from the U.S. it travels with the Annex VII information document and a contract with the EU recycler, with no prior consent

profile.headline: China ($996M, down 21.1% and less than half its 2020 level of $2.20B) buys only pulp now: kraft pulp, mostly fluff and other bleached softwood kraft ($773M), and dissolving pulp ($211M). U.S. pulp pays 10%, or 15% for buyers without an exclusion. U.S. recovered paper cannot enter: China has banned all solid-waste imports since January 1, 2021.
profile.mainProducts: Kraft (sulfate) pulp: NBSK, eucalyptus, fluff (4703) · Dissolving pulp (4702)

regulator.name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and General Administration of Customs (solid-waste import ban)
regulator.requirement: Wood pulp needs no product approval. Recovered paper cannot be imported in any form: Announcement No. 53 of 2020 bans imports of solid waste from January 1, 2021, and the licences for waste usable as raw material are no longer issued

profile.headline: India ($689M, down 2.6%) is the largest buyer of U.S. recovered paper (4707, $369M) and also buys kraft pulp (4703, $275M). It charges 2.5% on recovered paper and 5% on pulp; India has promised to cut tariffs on all U.S. industrial goods, but no rate or date is published.

regulator.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016), via DGFT import policy
regulator.requirement: India's import policy subjects waste imports to the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 and prohibits hazardous waste and anything contaminated with it, so recovered paper must be free of hazardous material (Basel entry B3020); the Indian importer handles the environment and customs formalities. assumptions: Each cell uses one representative six-digit subheading per heading, the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports: 4703.21 bleached softwood kraft (which includes fluff pulp), 4707.10 OCC, 4702.00 dissolving pulp, 4706.10 cotton linter pulp, 4704.29, 4701.00 and 4705.00. MFN rates are World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) applied rates for 2023, the latest year WITS holds, checked against the 2026 schedules of Canada (CBSA) and Japan; national 8–10-digit lines and national exemptions can differ.

The EU, Japan, Canada, Mexico, Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia charge 0% on every six-digit line of Chapter 47 (WITS 2023), so a trade agreement changes nothing there; Mexico and Canada are shown with the USMCA rate.

Canada's 4702 cell adds the 50% surtax of the United States Surtax Order (2026), SOR/2026-186, Schedule 3. Remission under the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025), such as for pulp used in Canadian manufacturing, is not netted out.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to China's 0% MFN rate. China's 2018–2019 counter-tariffs (5% on wood pulp, 20% on recycled-fiber pulp, 25% on recovered paper) are named in each basis but not added, because buyers can hold exclusions valid until December 31, 2026. Recovered paper is shown as banned: China stopped all solid-waste imports on January 1, 2021.
India's cells show basic customs duty only. Trade agreements that are signed or announced but not in force (India, Thailand, Malaysia, Taiwan) are not applied; see Tariff updates.
VAT and other internal taxes, the cost of EU deforestation due diligence and buyers' inspection and licence fees for recovered paper are not included.
